name: Muppim
overview: Muppim is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified as a (grand?)son of Benjamin and son of Bela. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, linking him to the early patriarchal narrative of Israel's sojourn in Egypt. His name appears in genealogical records that trace the lineage of the Benjaminite clans.
namesAndTitles: Muppim is also referred to by several variant names including Shephupham, Shuppim, and Shephuphan. The names Shephupham and Shephuphan possibly mean "serpent," suggesting a Hebrew root or symbolic meaning, while the other variants do not have specified meanings. None of these names are indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Muppim as a son of Bela and a descendant of Benjamin. He is also identified as the father of Iri and is inferred to have a brother named Maacah. These relationships place him firmly within the Benjaminite family line.
scriptureSignificance: Muppim's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records that document the descendants of Israel who migrated to Egypt, a foundational event in biblical history. As a member of the tribe of Benjamin, his lineage contributes to the understanding of the tribe's origins and its subdivisions, such as the Shuphamites. His multiple name variants reflect the transmission and preservation of tribal genealogies through different scriptural sources.
